function: Learned delay-Doppler estimation of targets from the estimated CFR matrix in a bistatic OFDM ISAC system with clutter and inter-cell interference (p. 1-2, 4).
system: Bistatic ISAC: ISAC Tx (precoding gain lumped into path gains, antennas not stated) sends OFDM; single-antenna UE senses Q=3 targets, 244 paths; 7 GHz (p. 1-2, 4).
method: LSTM stack with optional global attention (LSTMNet, LSTMNet + Att); supervised, MSE loss on normalized delay/Doppler labels, Adam, learning rate 1e-3, batch 256, 150 epochs (p. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulator: 3 targets, 12 clusters of 20 clutter points 'similar to' the 3GPP TR 38.901 cluster model, random positions and speeds, Gaussian path gains (p. 4).
test_conditions: Training SCINR and dataset size not stated; testing sweeps SCINR 0-20 dB with random target, clutter and UE positions and speeds in the same simulator (p. 4-5).
baselines: Classical: MUSIC, 2D-FFT, enhanced 2D-FFT (2D-FFT-e), SSTD. Learned: SNet-FNN (fully connected network inspired by [11]) and SNet-CNN, sized to similar complexity (p. 4-5).
metrics: RMSE of delay (ns) and Doppler (Hz) versus SCINR, CDF of errors at 10 dB; FLOPs, memory and run time; correct detection rate of Q (p. 4-5).
complexity: FLOPs, memory and run time (Table I): LSTMNet + Att 1.886 GFLOPs, 8.22 MB, 0.021 s; LSTMNet 1.884 GFLOPs, 7.5 MB, 0.020 s; compared with SNet-FNN/CNN (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "similar to the considered cluster model in 3GPP TR38.901 [16]". Only the cluster numerology (12 clusters, 20 points) is similar; positions, gains and Dopplers come from its own simulator, so not counted.
q2_support: p. 4: "We select a batch size of 256 and 150 epochs for both models." The paper gives no training SCINR, dataset size or test on an unseen scenario; results sweep SCINR only (Figs. 4-5), which does not count.
q3_support: p. 4: "compare them with four traditional baseline methods, namely MUSIC and 2D-FFT"; p. 5: "including a fully connected network called SensingNet" "inspired by the model in [11]", plus SNet-CNN; delay and Doppler RMSE in Figs. 4-5.
q4_support: p. 5: "the total number of floating point operations (FLOPs) in the inference stage, memory to store the model weights, and run times"; Table I: LSTMNet + Att 1.886 G FLOPs, 8.22 MB, 0.021 s.
q5_support: p. 4: "In this section, simulation results are presented for both detection and delay-Doppler estimation." Data come from its own simulator (p. 4); no code or data link is given.
notes: Borderline, flagged for the reviewer. (1) Function and area: the learned model estimates target delay and Doppler (sensing) in an ISAC system that also communicates (OFDM data to a UE), so it is not sensing alone in a system that does not communicate; it does not design beams, waveforms or resources. Included as area 5; if area 5 is read as design of beams, waveforms and resources only, exclude as function. The number of targets Q comes from existing detectors (Ratio Test, MDL, AIC, CA-CFAR, an AI-based one), not from the proposed network. (2) System: the UE has one antenna (p. 1); the ISAC Tx antenna count is not stated, but p. 2 mentions ISAC Tx precoding/beamforming gain in the path gain, so the link is not taken as single-antenna at both ends, although the simulated model is a scalar effective channel. (3) q1: the clutter is only similar to the 3GPP TR 38.901 cluster model (p. 4), not stated as built on it; reviewer to confirm. All 5 pages read, Table I and Figs. 3-5 viewed as images.
